title: Chapter 78: Night Flight 3
content:
Chapter 78

The crowd was paralyzed with terror. They had been dead certain they were about to meet a grisly end at the hands of the Yiling Laozu, destined to be reanimated as his mindless, flesh-eating puppets. But to their shock, Wei Wuxian couldn’t care less about messing with them. He gave the notice one last glance, left the mob sprawled in the dirt, and strolled off with his hands casually tucked behind his back.

He hadn’t bothered to call off the vengeful spirits, though. So the ground remained a sprawling mess of groaning bodies, with people writhing, whining in agony, and completely unable to get back on their feet.

Who knew how much time had crawled by when an arc of pale blue sword-glare swept through the air, and the crushing weight on everyone's backs instantly lifted. Someone gasped, "I can move!"

A few of them scrambled to their feet as best they could, just in time to see the streak of blue light curve back and glide cleanly into its scabbard.

The man holding it was strikingly young and handsome, draped in pristine white robes and wearing a forehead ribbon. His features were cold and solemn, his brow weighed down by a quiet, suffocating worry. He had moved with blinding speed, yet there wasn't a hint of haste in his bearing—even the hem of his robe fell without a single flutter.

The cultivator with the shattered legs gritted his teeth through the throbbing agony and rasped, "Han... Hanguang-jun!"

Lan Wangji strode over and knelt beside him, pressing his fingers against the fracture to assess the damage. Confirming it wasn't life-threatening, he rose to his feet. Before he could say a word, the cultivator blurted out, "Hanguang-jun, you just missed him! Wei Wuxian took off only moments ago!"

It was no secret that Gusu Lan’s Hanguang-jun had spent the past few days scouring the realm for Wei Wuxian—presumably to balance the ledger for the dozens of Lan disciples slaughtered on Koi Tower. The crowd piped up eagerly: "Right! He left barely half an hour ago!"

Lan Wangji asked, "What did he do? Where is he headed?"

The mob instantly broke into an avalanche of grievances: "He attacked us without rhyme or reason! Beat the living daylights out of us—he almost butchered every last one of us right here on the spot!"

Beneath his wide, snowy sleeve, Lan Wangji's fingers gave a faint, microscopic twitch, as if clenching into a fist, before relaxing just as quickly.

The wounded cultivator rushed to add, "He left a message, though! Said he’s heading straight for the Nightless City, planning to crash the Pledge Assembly and settle the score with the Four Great Clans!"

Ever since the fall of the Qishan Wen Clan, the main palaces of the Nightless City had crumbled into a magnificent, hollow graveyard of ruins.

Before the grand Hall of the Sun—perched atop the highest precipice of the entire fortress—stretched an impossibly vast square. Three soaring flagpoles had once dominated the front of the plaza. Today, two were snapped in half, while the lone survivor flew a battered, shredded sunburst flag soaked in drying blood.

Tonight, the square was packed to the brim with disciplined formations from sects across the land, each house’s standard snapping proudly in the bitter night wind. In front of the broken flagpoles stood a makeshift sacrificial altar. The clan leaders stood at the vanguard of their respective ranks, as Jin Guangyao personally served each of them a ceremonial cup of wine. Raising their cups in unison, the leaders tilted their wrists, letting the liquor bleed into the flagstones below.

As the wine sank into the earth, Jin Guangshan declared with solemn gravity, "Regardless of bloodline, regardless of name—this cup is offered to the brave souls of the clans who fell in battle."

Nie Mingjue’s voice was like stone: "May their heroic spirits endure forever."

Lan Xichen murmured softly, "May they find rest."

Jiang Cheng stood with a dark, storm-swept face, silently tipping his cup before clamping his jaw shut, refusing to utter a single syllable.

Next, Jin Guangyao stepped forward from the Lanling Jin ranks, presenting a square black iron coffer with both hands. Jin Guangshan hoisted the chest aloft with one arm and roared into the night: "Here lie the ashes of the Wen remnants!"

With that, he channeled his spiritual energy, shattering the iron box with his bare hands! The coffer burst into jagged shards, and an explosion of chalk-white powder billowed into the cold, desolate gale.

Their bones ground to dust, their ashes scattered to the wind!

A thunderous roar of triumphant cheers detonated through the crowd. Jin Guangshan raised both palms, gesturing for silence. As the clamor died down, his voice boomed across the stones once more: "Tonight, the ones whose ashes we scatter were the two ringleaders of the Wen scum! And tomorrow! Tomorrow it will be the rest of those Wen dogs, and—the Yiling Laozu, Wei Ying!"

A low chuckle suddenly sliced through his grand, sweeping rhetoric.

It was impossibly ill-timed, jarring and razor-sharp, snapping every head in the plaza upward in an instant.

The Hall of the Sun was a monumental structure boasting twelve grand roof ridges, each lined with eight traditional guardian beasts along its edge. Yet looking up, the crowd realized that one of the ridges was suddenly sporting nine. That derisive laugh had come straight from the rooftop!

The extra "guardian beast" shifted faintly. A heartbeat later, a black leather boot and the flutter of dark robes dangled off the eave, swinging lazily in the breeze.

Every sword hand snapped to its hilt in unison. Jiang Cheng’s pupils contracted to needles, the blue veins on the back of his hand bulging against his skin. Jin Guangshan’s face cycled violently between shock and rage as he barked, "Wei Ying! How dare you show your face here?!"

The figure spoke, the voice distinctly Wei Wuxian’s, yet carrying an eerie, hollow rasp: "Why wouldn't I dare? All of you combined—do you even break three thousand? Have you forgotten that back during the Sunshot Campaign, I took on five thousand men all by my lonesome? Besides, shouldn't my showing up make your lives easier? Saves you the trouble of trekking all the way out tomorrow just to scatter my ashes."

Several Qinghe Nie disciples had also lost their lives to Wen Ning’s rampage, prompting Nie Mingjue to sneer with pure contempt, "Arrogant brat."

Wei Wuxian countered, "Haven’t I always been this arrogant? Sect Leader Jin, slap your own face much? Who was the one who swore that if the Wen siblings offered their heads at Koi Tower, the ledger would be wiped clean? And who was just barking at the top of his lungs about burning me and the rest of the Wen survivors to ash tomorrow?"

Jin Guangshan spat, "One matter does not excuse another! The ambush at Qiongqi Path where you slaughtered over a hundred disciples of my Lanling Jin Sect is one debt! Unleashing Wen Ning to paint Koi Tower in blood is an entirely different—"

Wei Wuxian cut him off, voice dripping ice: "Then allow me to ask you, Sect Leader Jin: that ambush at Qiongqi Path—who was lying in wait, and who was the intended target? Who masterminded the slaughter, and who walked into the trap? When you strip it down to the bone, who was the one who picked the fight in the first place?!"

Shielded by the massive crowd, the disciples in the ranks found their courage, shouting up from the safety of the mob: "Even if Young Master Jin Zixun ambushed you first, you had no right to go that far! You slaughtered so many innocent lives!"

"Ah," Wei Wuxian drawled, breaking it down for him with mock helpfulness. "So when he tries to butcher me, he's allowed to go all-out without holding back, and if I drop dead, I'm just unlucky. But when I fight for my life, I have to tiptoe around, making sure I don't scratch this guy or bruise that guy, petrified of harming a single hair on his head? Basically, it’s fine for you lot to swarm and hunt me, but the second I hit back, I'm the villain. That about sum it up?"

Sect Leader Yao chimed in with self-righteous fury: "Hit back?! The hundred-plus men at Qiongqi Path and the thirty-odd cultivators at Koi Tower were completely innocent! Why did your retaliation have to drag them down with you?!"

Wei Wuxian fired right back: "And the fifty-odd Wen cultivators scraping by on the Burial Mounds were innocent too! Why did your retribution have to drag them into your crosshairs?!"

Another cultivator spat in disgust, "What grand debt of gratitude do you owe those Wen dogs that has you defending that scum to the death?!"

"There is no grand debt!" someone jeered from the ranks. "He just fancies himself some lone hero taking on the world! He thinks he's fighting some noble crusade, reveling in the delusion that defying the entire realm makes him look magnificent!"

Hearing those words, Wei Wuxian went dead silent.

The crowd below took his silence as a sign of weakness, pressing the attack: "When all is said and done, you were the one who struck first by placing that vile, cowardly blood curse on Jin Zixun!"

Wei Wuxian asked, "And pray tell, what shred of proof do you have that I cast that curse?"

The man choked on his words, momentarily stumped, before defensively snapping back, "Then what proof doyouhave that you didn't?!"

Wei Wuxian let out a sharp laugh. "Then let me flip the question: why couldn't it have been you? You don't have any proof you didn't cast it either, do you?"

The cultivator flushed with outrage. "Me?! How could you compare me to someone like you?! Stop twisting the truth and dodging the issue! You're the prime suspect! Do you think we don't know you and Jin Zixun have had bad blood for over a year?!"

Wei Wuxian’s tone chilled to the bone. "Who’s the one dodging the issue here? Exactly—if I wanted him dead, I would've slit his throat a year ago. Why wait until now? A fly like him isn't worth remembering for a year; I would’ve forgotten he existed in three days flat."

Sect Leader Yao was aghast. "...Wei Wuxian, oh Wei Wuxian, you really are a piece of work! In all my years, I have never laid eyes on a scoundrel so utterly devoid of reason... You slaughter a man, and then spit vile insults over his grave! Do you not possess a single ounce of empathy? Not a shred of remorse?!"

A storm of curses and slurs rained down on him from every direction, but Wei Wuxian took it all in stride.

Only pure, unadulterated fury could drown out the agonizing churn of other emotions tearing at his chest.

A cultivator standing near the front of his clan's formation spoke with heartbroken indignation: "Wei Ying, you have disappointed me to the core. To think I once held you in such high esteem, admiring you as a visionary trailblazer of a new path! Looking back on it now, it turns my stomach. From this moment on, we are sworn enemies!"

Wei Wuxian stared for a second, then doubled over in wild, breathless laughter.

He laughed so hard he could barely draw breath. "You admired me? If you admired me so damn much, how come I never saw your face while you were busy admiring me? Yet the second I'm the villain everyone wants dead, you jump right out to wave your little war banner and shout with the mob?!"

Tears of manic amusement prickled the corners of Wei Wuxian's eyes. "That admiration of yours is cheap as dirt. You say we're sworn enemies from this day forth? Wonderful! Does your eternal hatred or blood feud affect my life in the slightest? Your praise and your hatred are equally utterly worthless—how do you even have the nerve to stand there and shout them in my face?!"

Before the final word cleared his throat, a sudden, dull ache slammed into his chest, cutting off his breath.

He looked down. A fletched arrow was buried dead center between his ribs.

Tracking the trajectory, he looked toward the shot's origin. Standing in the ranks of a minor sect was a clean-faced young disciple, still frozen in his follow-through, his bowstring humming with lingering vibration.

Wei Wuxian could tell at a glance: the arrow was meant to be a lethal heart-shot. But the boy's archery was sloppy at best; the shot had lost momentum mid-flight, drifting off course and sinking into his ribs instead of piercing his vitals.

The cultivators flanking the boy stared in shock and horror, petrified by the sheer recklessness of their companion. Wei Wuxian lifted his head, dark malice bleeding into his features. With a sickening rip, he yanked the iron shaft from his own flesh and hurled it back down with brutal, raw force! A bloodcurdling shriek pierced the air—the rogue arrow slammed straight through the chest of the young disciple who had loosed it!

Beside him, another youth threw himself across the body, howling hysterically, "Brother! Brother!"

The minor sect’s formation dissolved into frantic chaos. The clan leader jabbed a shaking finger up at the roof, his voice trembling: "You... you... you heartless monster!"

Wei Wuxian pressed his palm against his bleeding chest, stemming the flow with casual indifference. "Heartless? If the kid had the guts to shoot me in the back, he should've been prepared for what happens if he missed. You've already branded me an irredeemable demon—did you honestly expect me to turn the other cheek?"

Jin Guangshan bellowed, "Form up! Set the arrays! He doesn't leave here alive tonight!"

That single command broke the deadlock. Scores of disciples mounted their swords, longbows drawn, swarming the roof of the great hall from all sides.

Finally. They made the first move!

A cold smirk curled Wei Wuxian's lips as he slipped Chenqing from his sash, raising the dark bamboo to his mouth. As the piercing, shrill wail of the flute tore through the night sky, pale, rotting arms burst through the paved stones of the square!

Corpses shattered the pristine white flagstones, clawing their way out from the depths of the earth. Cultivators who had barely gotten their swords airborne were violently dragged back to the ground. Perched atop the roof of the Hall of the Sun, Wei Wuxian played his flute horizontally, his dark eyes glinting with arctic malice under the moon. Looking down, the sea of sect robes churned like a boiling, multicolored cauldron—swirling in panic, scattering, converging. Aside from the Yunmeng Jiang formation, which remained completely untouched, every other clan was thrown into utter mayhem, sect leaders scrambling to shield their own disciples, completely unable to spare an attack for the man on the roof.

Right then, a clear, chiming chord cut across the haunting melody of Chenqing.

Wei Wuxian lowered the flute, glancing back. Perched on an opposing ridge sat a solitary figure, guqin resting across his knees, snowy white robes cutting a stark, jarring silhouette against the ink-black sky.

Wei Wuxian drawled with icy detachment, "Ah, Lan Zhan."

After greeting him, he brought the bamboo back to his lips. "You should know by now: your Song of Clarity doesn't work on me!"

Lan Wangji flipped the guqin onto his back and drew Bichen in one fluid motion, the blade streaking straight for Chenqing to shear the cursed instrument in two! Wei Wuxian twisted aside with agile grace, throwing his head back in wild, mocking laughter: "Fine, fine, fine! I knew it—we were bound to draw real steel and go at each other's throats sooner or later! You've never been able to stand the sight of me anyway, so come on! Let's have it!"

At those words, Lan Wangji’s strike hitched. "Wei Ying!"

The name was barked like a command, yet to anyone in their right mind, the tremor rattling Lan Wangji’s voice was unmistakable. But Wei Wuxian was far beyond reason. He was half-mad, his senses slipping away, every ounce of malice in the world magnified a thousandfold in his mind. He believed everyone despised him, and he despised everyone right back. Bring them on—he didn't care who it was, they were all the same to him.

Suddenly, cutting through the deafening roar of slaughter, a tiny, fragile voice reached his ears.

It was calling out: "A-Xian!"

The sound hit him like a bucket of freezing water, extinguishing the feral, raging fire in his chest in an instant.

Jiang Yanli?

When on earth did she get here?!

Terror seized his soul. Dropping Chenqing, he abandoned the duel with Lan Wangji, his voice cracking: "Shijie?!"

Jiang Cheng had heard it too. His face drained to a ghastly, bloodless white as he shouted into the fray, "Jie?! JIE! Where are you?! Where are you?!"

Wei Wuxian leaped down from the roof of the Hall of the Sun, screaming at the top of his lungs just like Jiang Cheng: "Shijie?! Shijie, where are you?! Where are you?! I can't see you!"

Ignoring the flurry of blades slashing toward him, he threw concussive palm strikes and frantic kicks to clear a path through the stampeding mob. Then, through a gap in the crowd, he caught a glimpse of her white mourning dress. Wei Wuxian shoved through the sea of bodies, fighting for every inch of ground. But the distance between them was vast, clogged by hundreds of panicked cultivators; neither he nor Jiang Cheng could close the gap in time. And worse, both of them suddenly noticed a walking corpse lurching upright directly behind her.

Half-decayed, dragging a rusted iron sword across the flagstones, the corpse was closing in on Jiang Yanli.

The bloodcurdling sight tore a hysterical scream from Wei Wuxian’s throat: "Get away! Get the hell away from her! Don't touch her!"

Jiang Cheng roared, "Get it off her!"

He hurled Sandu with all his might, the purple sword-glare whistling straight for the corpse. But mid-flight, a stray blade from another cultivator knocked it wildly off course. The more frantic Wei Wuxian’s mind became, the more his control frayed at the seams; completely ignoring his frantic mental directives, the corpse raised its rusted blade, swinging down toward Jiang Yanli!

Wei Wuxian lost what was left of his mind, sprinting wildly: "Stop! Stop, damn you, stop!"

Every cultivator on the field was too busy fighting for their own lives against the undead to notice anyone else in peril. The rusted blade came crashing down, slicing clean through Jiang Yanli’s back!

She crumpled straight onto the stone.

Looming over her, the corpse hoisted its sword for a second strike—just as a streak of azure light cleaved its upper torso clean in half!

Lan Wangji landed in the square, catching Bichen on its return arc. Wei Wuxian and Jiang Cheng finally broke through the crowd, neither having the presence of mind to even mutter a word of thanks. Jiang Cheng scooped Jiang Yanli into his arms, while Lan Wangji intercepted Wei Wuxian, grabbing him by the collar and hoisting him up, his voice dangerously sharp: "Wei Ying! Call off the corpses!"

Wei Wuxian couldn't register anything else. He didn't see Lan Wangji’s face, couldn't see the crimson veins spider-webbing across his pale eyes, nor the raw redness rimming his lids. His only thought was Jiang Yanli. With bloodshot eyes, he violently shoved Lan Wangji away, throwing himself onto the dirt. Knocked off-balance, Lan Wangji steadied himself and looked at him. Before he could make another move, distant shrieks for help tore through the air, and forcing his gaze away, he leaped back into the fray to save lives.

Jiang Yanli’s back was drenched in blood. Her eyes were shut, but she was still breathing. Jiang Cheng pulled his trembling hand back from her pulse, letting out a ragged breath of relief, before rearing back and planting a brutal fist straight into Wei Wuxian's jaw!

"What the hell is this?!" Jiang Cheng snarled. "Didn't you swear you had everything under control?! Didn't you swear nothing would go wrong?!"

Splayed across the flagstones, Wei Wuxian stared blankly. "...I don't know."

Despair tore his voice to shreds: "...I can't control them... I can't hold them back..."

Right then, Jiang Yanli gave a faint twitch. Jiang Cheng pulled her closer, his words tumbling out in a frantic scramble: "Jie! You're fine, you're going to be fine! How does it feel? It's okay, it's just a flesh wound, I'm taking you out of here right now..."

He moved to lift her, but Jiang Yanli whispered weakly, "...A-Xian."

A violent shudder ran through Wei Wuxian’s spine. "Shijie, I... I'm right here."

Jiang Yanli slowly parted her dark, gentle eyes, and sheer panic seized Wei Wuxian's chest.

She forced out each syllable with immense effort: "...A-Xian. Earlier... why did you run off so fast... I didn't even get the chance to look at you, or say a word to you..."

His heart hammered violently against his ribs.

He still didn't have the courage to look at her face—especially now, covered in grime and drying blood, looking horrifyingly like Jin Zixuan at the very end.

And he was terrified to hear what she would say next.

She murmured, "I... came here to tell you..."

Tell him what?

That it was fine?

That she didn't hate him?

That nothing was wrong?

That she didn't blame him for killing Jin Zixuan?

Impossible.

Yet words of bitter hatred and blame were things she could never bring herself to say to him either.

She didn't know what she was supposed to say to him under the heavens.

All she knew was that she had to see her little brother one last time.

With a soft, aching sigh, Jiang Yanli whispered, "A-Xian, you... stop this now. Don't... don't do this anymore..."

Wei Wuxian nodded frantically. "Okay. I'll stop. I'm stopping."

He raised Chenqing to his lips, keeping his head bowed as he began to play. He burned through every scrap of willpower he possessed just to steady his frayed spirit. This time, the corpses finally stopped ignoring his commands; one by one, issuing low, gurgling rasps from their throats like grumbling hounds, they slowly sank to the earth.

In the distance, Lan Wangji’s blade paused. He looked back toward them, then pivoted, resuming his strikes to rescue disciples trapped in the fray.

Suddenly, Jiang Yanli’s eyes snapped wide. With a burst of inexplicable, frantic strength, she shoved Wei Wuxian with all her might!

The push sent him sprawling across the stones. By the time he lifted his head, a gleaming steel blade had pierced clean through her throat.

Holding the hilt was the young cultivator who had been weeping over the archer's body earlier. He was still bawling, sobbing through blurred, tear-streaked eyes: "Wei-dog! This strike is for my brother!"

Wei Wuxian sat paralyzed on the filthy flagstones, staring in stunned disbelief at Jiang Yanli, whose head had slumped sideways, a torrent of dark blood gushing from her neck.

Just a second ago, he had been waiting for her to speak, waiting for her to hand down his final sentence.

Beside him, Jiang Cheng was utterly frozen, still cradling his sister's limp frame, his mind completely blank.

An agonizing, bloodcurdling shriek tore from Wei Wuxian’s lungs.

Lan Wangji ran a corpse through and whipped his head around, his face draining of all color.

Only then did the youth realize he had struck the wrong target. He ripped the blade free, sending a spray of arterial crimson across the air, stumbling backward in blind terror: "...N-no, it wasn't me, it wasn't... I was trying to kill Wei Wuxian, I was avenging my brother... She threw herself into the blade!"

Wei Wuxian materialized before him like a ghost, his hand clamping around the boy's throat. Sect Leader Yao raised his blade, bellowing, "Demon, let him go!"

Lan Wangji abandoned every scrap of his legendary composure. Shoving aside anyone in his path, he sprinted toward Wei Wuxian. But before he was halfway there, Wei Wuxian snapped the boy's neck with his bare hands right in front of the entire world.

Another cultivator roared in fury, "You! You—first you got Jiang Fengmian and his wife killed, and now you've driven your own Shijie to her grave! You brought this entirely on yourself, yet you dare blame others?! Refusing to repent, continuing your senseless butchery—you are utterly beyond redemption!"

Yet no amount of curses or condemnations could reach Wei Wuxian anymore.

As if possessed by another soul, he reached into his sleeves with both hands, pulling out two halves of an object, and fitted them together before the gaping eyes of the crowd.

One top, one bottom, they locked into a single entity with a sharp, resonant, and chilling metallic clang.

Resting it flat upon his open palm, Wei Wuxian hoisted it high into the night sky.

The Yin Tiger Tally!
